newsitem.title: UK: Celsis introduces new water quality test.
newsitem.headline: Celsis introduces new water quality test.

text.p: Celsis International Plc on Thursday said it and the Belgian university of Ghent have developed a fast and easy to use method to test water quality.
The company said its saw a market for this type of test, called ColicountTM, of over 250 million stg per year.
The new test detects the presence of Coliforms and the poisonous E Coli bacteria, which could result from faecal contamination and which can cause tummy upset.

A particularly virulent E Coli strain -- E Coli 0157 -- killed 19 elderly people late last year and early this year. This strain is usually transmitted via undercooked meat, but is unlikely to be found in water.
Colicount, which is still undergoing field trials, meets the need for a rapid testing method in case of emergencies when contamination threatens widespread water supplies, Celsis said.
The test, which is expected to hit the market later this year, is about twice as fast as the speediest systems currently available, the Cambridge-based firm said.
